claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be prepared in a fully homogenized high-temperature BCC state.
Persistence of the high-temperature BCC state in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by kinetic limitations.
Transformation from the BCC state requires atomic partitioning.
Cr partitioning is particularly important to the transformation.
At temperatures below the high-temperature BCC stability regime, the alloy is thermodynamically unstable toward formation of lower-temperature equilibrium phases.
Cr diffusion at the proposed annealing temperature is sluggish.
Limited Cr diffusion restricts nucleation of the equilibrium phase or phases.
The activation energy for Cr diffusion is high enough to delay transformation at the annealing temperature.
Extended annealing permits sufficient atomic partitioning to overcome the kinetic or nucleation barrier.
Once sufficient partitioning occurs, equilibrium phase or phases emerge.
Extended annealing will produce a larger fraction of newly transformed phases than short-time annealing at the same temperature.
A short-time annealed sample is expected to exhibit minimal phase transformation.
The proposed mechanism applies under isothermal conditions below the nominal BCC stability limit where thermodynamic driving forces for transformation coexist with restricted atomic mobility.
Increasing annealing duration at a fixed temperature is the proposed controlled intervention for changing the extent of atomic partitioning.
Phase fractions and Cr distributions are proposed as measurable responses to annealing duration.
No statistically significant increase in equilibrium-phase fraction with annealing duration is specified as the falsifying result.
